chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Uzafir, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Know that the optional prayer is in the status of a gift; whenever it is brought, it is accepted.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of the optional prayer (Nafilah) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses the metaphor of a gift (hadiyah) to highlight the divine generosity in accepting voluntary prayers, which are not obligatory but serve to draw the believer closer to God. In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith underscores the spiritual merit of nafl prayers as acts of love and devotion rather than mere duty, reinforcing the concept that God eagerly accepts the efforts of His servants. This teaching encourages consistency in voluntary worship, viewing it as a means of spiritual elevation and intimacy with the Divine.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Amro Bin Usman, from Muhammad Bin Uzafir, from Umar Bin Yazeed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Know, that the optional (Salāt) is at the status of a gift. Whenever one comes up with it, is Accepted’.
en.sarwar: 14. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthman from Muhammad ibn ‘Adhafir from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Optional Salah (prayer) is like present; whenever given is accepted.’”
